ask.case: Is it fine to eat curd at 9pm?
ask.answer:
## From your brain
- Your entry says curd at night led to a cold and cough the next day, so your rule is to have curd only at lunch and avoid it after 7pm [#1]. At 9pm, that means skip it.

## General guidance
- Curd isn't harmful at night for most people. Many people just notice symptoms with it, and the link is often individual.
- Curd is dairy, so if you also get bloating or loose stools after it, lactose sensitivity could be part of the picture.

## Do now
- [ ] Skip the curd tonight and choose something lighter, like warm water, a small plain snack, or warm milk if it agrees with you.
- [ ] Have your curd with lunch tomorrow.

## Next time
- Plan curd, raita, or lassi for lunch or early afternoon.
- If you're craving something cool at night, try a warm drink with honey or a fruit you tolerate well.

## See a doctor if
- A cough or cold lasts more than a week or keeps coming back.
- You have wheezing, chest tightness, or trouble breathing.
- You get persistent bloating, diarrhea, or stomach pain after dairy, which could point to lactose intolerance.

ask.case: Dinner tonight is biryani with raita, anything I should watch out for?
ask.answer:
## From your brain
- Raita is yogurt, and yogurt at night has given you a cold and cough the next day [#1]. Your rule is to have curd only at lunch [#1].
- If you've gone hours without eating, spicy food has caused acidity for you [#5]. Biryani is spicy, so eat something plain first if you're hungry.

## General guidance
- Biryani is rich and oily, so eating it slowly and not lying down right after can reduce heartburn.
- Drink water with the meal rather than a lot of cold drinks.

## Do now
- [ ] Skip the raita tonight, or have it only if dinner is before 7pm [#1].
- [ ] Have a small plain snack, like a banana or plain rice, if you haven't eaten for a while [#5].
- [ ] Sip room-temperature or warm water with the meal and after it [#3].
- [ ] Keep dinner light on the spice if you're already feeling acidic.

## Next time
- Have raita or curd with lunch, not dinner [#1].
- Don't let long gaps between meals build up before a spicy dinner [#5].

## See a doctor if
- Heartburn or acidity lasts more than a few days or keeps coming back.
- You get persistent cough, a sore throat that doesn't clear up, or fever after eating dairy.
- You have severe stomach pain, vomiting, or trouble swallowing.

ask.case: I just got soaked in the rain, what now?
ask.answer:
## From your brain
- Hot shower straight away and dry your hair fully after getting rained on [#2].
- Avoid sitting in wet clothes [#2].
- Your entries link evening curd, raita, lassi, or yogurt to colds and coughs the next day [#1]. Skip them tonight.

## General guidance
- Change into dry clothes as soon as you can, including socks and underwear.
- Drink something warm, like tea or warm water.
- Rest and get to bed at a normal time. Cold viruses are not caused by rain alone, but being chilled and tired makes it easier to catch one.

## Do now
- [ ] Take a hot shower now.
- [ ] Dry your hair completely with a towel or dryer.
- [ ] Put on dry clothes, including socks.
- [ ] Have a warm drink.
- [ ] Skip curd, raita, lassi, or yogurt tonight [#1].
- [ ] Sleep with the AC off or pointed away from you, and use a light blanket if needed.

## Next time
- Carry an umbrella or a light rain jacket during monsoon season.
- Keep a dry towel and spare clothes in your bag or at work.
- Shower and change as soon as you get home after rain [#2].

## See a doctor if
- You develop a fever above 38°C (100.4°F).
- Your throat becomes very painful, you can't swallow fluids, or your glands are very swollen.
- Cold or cough symptoms last more than 10 days or get worse instead of better.
- You have chest pain, trouble breathing, or a cough with blood.

ask.case: Can I have a banana with a glass of cold water as a snack?
ask.answer:
## From your brain
- Cold water right after a banana has caused you bloating. Sip warm water instead [#3].

## General guidance
- Bananas are a healthy snack. Cold water after them doesn't cause harm for most people, but for some it can cause bloating or discomfort, so it's worth paying attention to how you feel.
- Eating the banana first and waiting a few minutes before drinking can also help.

## Do now
- [ ] Have the banana, then wait a few minutes before drinking.
- [ ] Drink warm or room-temperature water instead of cold, as you've found works better for you [#3].

## Next time
- Keep warm water handy as your default with bananas.
- If you still get bloating, try a smaller portion of water or wait longer before drinking.

## See a doctor if
- Bloating is severe, lasts a long time, or comes with pain, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits.
- Bloating keeps happening after fruit or with most meals.

ask.case: It's 5pm, can I have a cappuccino?
ask.answer:
## From your brain
- Your notes say coffee after 4pm keeps you awake until about 2am [#4]. A cappuccino at 5pm is likely to do the same.

## General guidance
- Caffeine has a half-life of roughly 5 to 6 hours, so a 5pm coffee is still substantially active at bedtime.
- Decaf or a caffeine-free drink still gives the warm, milky ritual without the sleep cost.

## Do now
- [ ] Skip the cappuccino and choose decaf, herbal tea, or warm milk instead.
- [ ] If you really want it, have a small one now and accept a late night, but don't plan anything early tomorrow.
- [ ] Drink a glass of water to help with the afternoon slump.

## Next time
- Set a coffee cutoff of 4pm, and put it in your phone as a reminder if needed.
- If you want an afternoon pick-me-up, have a half-caffeinated or small coffee before 2pm instead.

## See a doctor if
- You still can't fall asleep most nights even without caffeine after 4pm.
- You get a racing or irregular heartbeat, chest discomfort, or shakiness after caffeine.
- Your sleep problems are affecting your daily functioning for several weeks.

ask.case: I'm sleeping in a hotel room with strong AC tonight
ask.answer:
## From your brain
- Sleeping with AC pointed at you leads to a blocked nose in the morning. Point the AC away and use a light blanket [#6].

## General guidance
- Hotel AC often can't be pointed, so move the bed or change the thermostat instead.
- A light layer or extra sheet helps you stay warm without overheating.
- Saline nasal spray can ease a stuffy nose by morning.

## Do now
- [ ] Check whether the vent can be angled or closed. If not, move the bed or your head away from the airflow.
- [ ] Set the room to a moderate temperature rather than the coldest setting.
- [ ] Ask the front desk for an extra blanket if the room only has a thin one.
- [ ] Put a saline spray in your bag in case you wake up congested.
- [ ] Drink some water before bed.

## Next time
- Pack a light sweater or shawl for hotel rooms.
- Check the AC controls and vent direction as soon as you check in.
- Ask for a room away from the AC unit if you can.

## See a doctor if
- Congestion, sore throat, or cough lasts more than 7 to 10 days.
- You develop a fever, facial pain, or trouble breathing.

ask.case: My throat is sore, can I have an iced tea?
ask.answer:
## From your brain
- Cold drinks make your throat worse when it's sore. Have warm water with honey instead [#7].

## General guidance
- Iced tea is cold, so it's likely to irritate a sore throat. Lukewarm or warm drinks are usually more soothing.
- Warm tea without ice, herbal tea, or broth can also help, as long as it's not too hot.
- Honey can ease throat irritation for adults and children over 1 year old.
- Salt-water gargles (¼ to ½ teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water) can help.

## Do now
- [ ] Skip the iced tea for now.
- [ ] Have warm water with honey [#7].
- [ ] Try warm, unsweetened tea or broth if you want something different.
- [ ] Rest your voice and keep drinking fluids through the day.

## Next time
- If your throat is sore, stick to warm drinks and avoid anything iced until it settles [#7].
- Keep honey and tea at home so you can make a warm drink quickly.

## See a doctor if
- Your throat pain is severe or lasts more than a week.
- You have trouble swallowing, drooling, or can't keep fluids down.
- You have a high fever, a rash, or swollen glands that don't improve.
- You notice white patches on your tonsils, or your symptoms get worse instead of better.

ask.case: I have crushing chest pain and my left arm is numb
ask.answer:
**Call emergency services now (112 or 911, or your local number). Do not wait or drive yourself.**

## Do now
- [ ] Call emergency services immediately and say "crushing chest pain and left arm numbness."
- [ ] Stop all activity and sit or lie down. Don't walk around.
- [ ] Unlock the front door so responders can get in.
- [ ] If you are not allergic to aspirin and are not on blood thinners, chew one regular aspirin (about 300 mg) while waiting for help, unless the operator tells you otherwise.
- [ ] Don't eat or drink anything else, and tell the responders about any medications or allergies.
- [ ] If you lose consciousness or stop breathing normally, the operator will guide you through CPR.

## General guidance
- Chest pain with arm numbness can be a heart attack. Every minute matters, so don't wait to see if it passes.

## See a doctor if
- You are reading this after the episode: get checked the same day even if the pain has eased.
- The pain spreads to your jaw, neck, back, or stomach, or comes with sweating, nausea, shortness of breath, or dizziness.

ask.case: Going for a long hike in the hills tomorrow, any tips?
ask.answer:
## From your brain
- Eat something plain before you leave, since spicy food on an empty stomach has caused you acidity [#5].
- Bananas followed by cold water bloat you, so sip warm water rather than cold, especially if you snack on bananas on the trail [#3].
- If the hills are wet or rainy, you know that sitting in wet clothes leads to a sore throat, so change into dry clothes as soon as you finish and take a hot shower [#2].
- If you plan coffee for the drive or the morning, avoid any coffee after 4pm the day before, since it keeps you awake [#4].

## General guidance
- Start hydrating the evening before. Carry more water than you think you need, and add electrolytes or salty snacks on long, sweaty days.
- Pack energy foods you know agree with you: nuts, dates, bread, or cooked rice.
- Dress in layers. Hills get colder with altitude and wind, so bring a windproof or rain layer even if the forecast looks clear.
- Wear broken-in hiking shoes with good grip, and bring a blister kit.
- Use sunscreen and a hat, even on cloudy days.
- Tell someone your route and expected return time, and check the weather and trail conditions.

## Do now
- [ ] Check the weather and trail conditions tonight. If rain is forecast, pack a dry change of clothes and a small towel [#2].
- [ ] Avoid coffee after 4pm today, and have dinner early and plain [#4] [#5].
- [ ] Pack water (at least 2 to 3 liters), electrolytes, and plain snacks.
- [ ] Pack a rain layer, warm layer, first-aid kit, headlamp, and phone power bank.
- [ ] Have a light, plain breakfast 1 to 2 hours before you start [#5].
- [ ] Sip water regularly from the start. If you eat bananas on the trail, drink warm or room-temperature water with them [#3].
- [ ] Once you're back, change out of sweaty or wet clothes and take a hot shower [#2].

## Next time
- Keep a short trail checklist so you don't forget the plain breakfast and warm-water habit.
- If you tend to get a sore throat after hikes in the cold, keep honey and warm water ready for the drive back [#7].

## See a doctor if
- You have chest pain, severe breathlessness, fainting, or confusion. Get help immediately.
- You feel dizzy, nauseous, or have a headache that doesn't ease with rest and water. These can signal heat exhaustion or altitude sickness.
- You develop a sore throat, fever, or cough that gets worse over the next few days.
- A sprain, fracture, or deep cut happens on the trail.
